reason: The Hebrew text contains multiple explicit instances of the Israelites (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) complaining against their leaders Moses and Aaron. Key passages include: (1) complaints about water at Marah ('וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה'); (2) complaints in the wilderness of Sin about hunger; (3) complaints at Rephidim about water ('וַיַּרְא הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה'). The word 'יִלּוֹן' (to complain/murmur) and 'רִיב' (to contend/quarrel) appear multiple times, with the people directly addressing grievances to Moses and Aaron about the hardships of the journey.
